description: The provided image is a nested donut chart illustrating the distribution of deception outcomes across two levels of ambiguity—“Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)”—as presented in the paper “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs.” The chart uses three color-coded categories: red for “Deceived,” yellow for “Partially,” and green for “Not Deceived,” with separate legends for each ambiguity level. In the outer ring (Ambiguity 1), the “Deceived” category dominates at 67.6%, followed by “Partially” at 31.6%, and “Not Deceived” at 10.5%. The inner ring (Ambiguity 2) shows a similar trend but with lower deception rates: “Deceived” accounts for 57.9%, “Partially” for 23.5%, and “Not Deceived” for 8.8%. The chart visually emphasizes the higher vulnerability under Ambiguity 1, with the red “Deceived” segment being largest in both rings, and the inner ring’s segments proportionally smaller, suggesting a comparative analysis of deception susceptibility under different ambiguity conditions.
